title: Extension-by-zero criterion for Noetherian cohomology
statement: Let X be a topological space and d\geq 0 an integer. Assume (1) X is quasi-compact, (2) the quasi-compact opens form a basis of X, (3) the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, and (4) H^p(X,j_!\underline{\mathbf Z}_U)=0 for all p>d and every quasi-compact open j:U \to X, where \underline{\mathbf Z}_U is the constant abelian sheaf on U [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and j_! is extension by zero [lem-sc-topological-extension-by-zero-stalks]. Then H^p(X,F)=0 for all p>d and every abelian sheaf F on X [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

source.place: Lemma 02UX (cohomology-lemma-vanishing-reduction), in the proof of Proposition 02UZ

proof.text: Apply the finite-generation and one-section quotient reduction [lem-sc-cohomology-reduction-constant-subsheaves]. Its compact-open vanishing hypothesis is the given hypothesis. It remains to prove vanishing above d for every finitely generated subsheaf K of the constant integer sheaf.

Apply [lem-sc-constant-subsheaf-finite-filtration] to K, using the compact-intersection hypothesis. Obtain monomorphisms between consecutive terms, a zero initial term, final term isomorphic to K, and successive cokernels Q_i. For each Q_i the supplied short exact sequence has first two terms isomorphic to compact-open integer extensions. In degree q>d its middle term cohomology and the first term cohomology in degree q+1 both vanish. Mathlib Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃ therefore gives vanishing for Q_i.

Induct over the finite filtration. The initial term has zero cohomology because an additive Ext functor preserves zero objects. For each monomorphism f_i, the canonical sequence F_i to F_{i+1} to cokernel(f_i) is short exact. Its cokernel is isomorphic to Q_i. Vanishing for F_i and Q_i implies vanishing for F_{i+1} by Mathlib Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂. Transfer the final vanishing through the isomorphism to K, supplying the last hypothesis of Step 1. All isomorphism transports are maps of the cohomology functor.
